detail: A DEVICE ARRIVES NAMED ---- 17 Nov 2026, reading his own key list: "just wondering why it registered like that in the first place?" Because this label was a two-line guess at navigator.userAgent, and that string is thinner than it looks. A Mac says "Macintosh; Intel Mac OS X 10_15_7": no phone, no browser name, and an OS version Apple froze for privacy years ago - so it fell through to the literal word "browser". Android says "Android 10" and never the handset model; the model lives in userAgentData, which nothing asked for.

What changed, and what did not: the label names the browser and the platform it can honestly know, and asks the browser for the handset model where a browser will answer. It never invents a model, never prints macOS's frozen version as if it were true, and never waits on a hint that does not come back - a model is a courtesy, never a condition of enrolling. The name is still frozen at enrolment.
